blocks.c: Minus nine was not a floor. Minus nine was a warehouse, and it went further than my torch went in every direction, and it was full of shelving, and the shelving was full of boxes, and every box had a label.
TAM, PEREGRINE — 2011. Two boxes, and one of them was open, and I did not look in it, and I am glad.
The photocopier was somewhere off to the left, chunking away, unattended, spitting sheets into a tray.
And forty feet in, on the end of a rack, at chest height, there was a single box with a label so new that the ink had not gone matte.
It had three things in it.

A small paper packet, the kind pharmacies use, with something granular in it that smelled — and I got this immediately, and it went through me like a nail — exactly like my coffee. The way I take it. Took it.
A street sign. A real one, aluminium, bolt holes and all, and I read the name on it and I still could not attach it to my own childhood, but I could feel the shape where it fit.
I put all three in my bag.
I want to say that I stood there and thought carefully about whether taking things from an inventory was a good idea.
What actually happened is that the photocopier stopped.
